question: A triathlete competes in a triathlon in which the swimming, biking, and running segments are all of the same length. The triathlete swims at a rate of \(3\) kilometers per hour, bikes at a rate of \(20\) kilometers per hour, and runs at a rate of \(10\) kilometers per hour. Which of the following is closest to the triathlete’s average speed, in kilometers per hour, for the entire race?
solution:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Multiplying all segment lengths by the same positive factor multiplies their travel times by that factor too, leaving the average speed unchanged. We can therefore use \(60\) kilometers for each segment to make the times whole numbers.

Time equals distance divided by speed, so the swimming, biking, and running times are respectively
\[
\frac{60}{3}=20,\qquad
\frac{60}{20}=3,\qquad
\frac{60}{10}=6
\]
hours. The total distance is \(180\) kilometers, and the total time is \(20+3+6=29\) hours. Thus the average speed is
\[
\frac{180}{29}=6+\frac{6}{29}\text{ km/h}.
\]
Since \(0<\frac{6}{29}<\frac12\), the average speed lies between \(6\) and \(6.5\). The closest listed speed is \(6\) kilometers per hour, choice \(D\).
